scenario_text: Your university has been responding to digital demands in teaching and learning on a case-by-case basis. Several departments have adopted different tools independently. The senior leadership team has recently discussed the need for a more coordinated approach. A deputy vice-chancellor asks you: 'Where are we on digital strategy for teaching and learning?'

response_options.text: We have a clear digital strategy for teaching and learning that was approved last year and is being implemented across all faculties
response_options.explanation: This would indicate Intentional if true, but the scenario describes no approved strategy

response_options.text: We recognise the need and are actively developing a digital strategy for teaching and learning with identified priorities and a governance proposal
response_options.explanation: Active development of a purposeful strategy with governance indicates transition toward Intentional

response_options.text: We've been meaning to write a strategy but haven't found the time. Meanwhile, departments are managing things in their own way
response_options.explanation: Acknowledged need without action and devolved ad-hoc activity is Incidental

response_options.text: Our institutional strategic plan mentions digital transformation and we reference that when departments ask for guidance
response_options.explanation: A passing mention in a broader strategy without specific objectives, owners, or resources for teaching and learning is not a purposeful strategy. This is the 'we have a plan' attractive nuisance

scenario_text: Your university's board has asked for an update on how digital technology supports teaching and learning. You discover that while several successful digital initiatives exist across the institution, they were each initiated by individual champions with no central coordination. The board wants to know what the institutional approach is.

response_options.text: We have a coordinated institutional approach with a strategy document, dedicated budget, and a committee overseeing digital in teaching and learning
response_options.explanation: This describes Intentional with formal strategy, resources, and governance

response_options.text: We have some excellent initiatives and we're now developing a formal strategy to bring them together under a coherent plan
response_options.explanation: Transitioning from ad-hoc to purposeful planning indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We have a lot of innovative activity happening organically. Our approach is to let a thousand flowers bloom and learn from what works
response_options.explanation: Framing lack of strategy as deliberate emergent innovation is a common attractive nuisance. Organic activity without coordination is Incidental

response_options.text: We don't really have an institutional approach yet. Individual departments have done their own thing based on local needs
response_options.explanation: Honest acknowledgement of no institutional approach is Incidental

scenario_text: Your university approved a digital teaching and learning strategy 18 months ago. The strategy has clear objectives and a steering group meets quarterly. However, implementation varies dramatically across faculties. Two faculties are well advanced, three have barely started, and the remaining faculties fall somewhere in between. A new PVC asks how well the strategy is being implemented.

response_options.text: The strategy is fully embedded. All faculties have adopted it and are implementing it consistently with local adaptation
response_options.explanation: This would indicate Integrated if true, but the scenario contradicts this

response_options.text: We have strong pockets of implementation and we're working to bring all faculties up to the standard of our leading areas
response_options.explanation: 'Strong pockets' with inconsistent implementation across the institution is characteristic of Intentional. The attractive nuisance is that activity in multiple locations feels like integration

response_options.text: Implementation is uneven. We have the strategy but we haven't yet achieved consistent cross-institutional adoption with proper governance and accountability
response_options.explanation: Honest assessment of uneven implementation describes Intentional

response_options.text: All faculties have operational plans that reference the institutional strategy, with locally adapted targets, and we report on progress to the board termly
response_options.explanation: Faculty-level plans aligned to institutional strategy with regular reporting indicates Integrated

scenario_text: Your university has invested in a central digital teaching and learning team of six staff who develop and support digital initiatives. The team runs projects across faculties, but each project requires negotiation with individual faculty leaders for access and cooperation. The team reports to the PVC Education but has no formal authority over faculty-level decisions.

response_options.text: Having a dedicated central team with a clear reporting line shows we have an integrated approach to digital teaching and learning
response_options.explanation: A central team without governance authority over faculties and without faculty-level adoption of institutional strategy operates in an Intentional model. The attractive nuisance is equating central team existence with integration

response_options.text: We have purposeful investment in digital teaching and learning but the central team operates somewhat independently from faculty planning. We need stronger governance to achieve integration
response_options.explanation: Purposeful investment without cross-institutional governance is accurately Intentional

response_options.text: The central team's work is governed by a cross-institutional board with faculty representation, and faculty plans are required to align with the digital strategy
response_options.explanation: If this were true it would indicate Integrated, but the scenario describes a team negotiating cooperation

response_options.text: Our digital teaching and learning activity is still at an early stage with no real coordination between the centre and faculties
response_options.explanation: This understates the scenario, which does describe purposeful investment

scenario_text: Your university has a well-functioning digital teaching and learning strategy that is implemented consistently across all faculties. Governance is strong, KPIs are reported regularly, and the institution has achieved solid results. The PVC Education wants to know whether the institution can now be considered sector-leading.

response_options.text: We regularly benchmark against Russell Group peers and ensure our approach matches best practice. We've adopted several approaches we learned from peer institutions
response_options.explanation: Benchmarking by adopting approaches from others is characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that benchmarking activity feels like sector leadership, but copying good practice is not the same as setting it

response_options.text: We review our strategy annually based on data, run a horizon scanning function, publish our approaches, and other institutions regularly visit to learn from us
response_options.explanation: Evidence-based annual review, horizon scanning, publication, and peer recognition indicates Optimised

response_options.text: Our implementation is strong and consistent but we recognise we're implementing established good practice rather than innovating ahead of the sector
response_options.explanation: Honest assessment of implementing good practice without leading innovation is Integrated

response_options.text: We've won a national award for one of our digital teaching and learning initiatives and were featured in a trade publication
response_options.explanation: A single award for a specific initiative does not indicate systematic sector leadership. The attractive nuisance is equating one recognition with Optimised maturity

scenario_text: Your university has strong digital teaching and learning governance and consistent implementation. The sector is now grappling with a new technological development that could significantly impact teaching and learning. Several peer institutions are starting to respond.

response_options.text: We formed an expert panel six months ago to assess the implications and have already piloted approaches. We published a briefing paper that three peer institutions have since adopted
response_options.explanation: Proactive assessment, early piloting, and sector contribution through publication indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're watching what leading institutions are doing and plan to adopt best practice once it becomes clearer what works
response_options.explanation: Waiting to adopt others' practices is reactive benchmarking, characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that this feels prudent and strategic

response_options.text: We've established a task force to develop our response and are developing a pilot programme informed by sector guidance
response_options.explanation: Developing a response informed by others indicates Integrated responding effectively, not Optimised leading

response_options.text: We've been preparing for this for over a year through our horizon scanning process and have an institutional position and implementation plan ready
response_options.explanation: Anticipating the development through horizon scanning indicates Optimised proactive strategic maturity

scenario_text: Your university is assessing digital skills readiness among academic staff. A survey reveals that 15% of academic staff are highly digitally capable and actively innovating, while 60% use basic digital tools but avoid anything more advanced. The remaining 25% actively resist using digital tools. No institutional development programme for digital skills in teaching and learning exists.

response_options.text: We clearly have digital capability. 15% of our academic staff are highly skilled and leading innovation in teaching and learning
response_options.explanation: Concentrated expertise in a small minority without institutional development is the hallmark of Incidental. The attractive nuisance is celebrating individual champions as institutional capability

response_options.text: We need to start investing in digital skills for academic staff. We're planning a development programme targeting the 60% in the middle
response_options.explanation: Planning purposeful investment in workforce development indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We don't have an institutional programme. Skills are developed through informal peer learning and self-study
response_options.explanation: Informal, self-directed development without institutional programme is Incidental

response_options.text: We've launched a targeted digital capabilities programme for academic staff with modules mapped to role requirements, and we're tracking participation
response_options.explanation: A targeted, tracked programme indicates Intentional

scenario_text: Your university is recruiting for a senior role in teaching and learning. The job description does not mention digital competencies. The hiring manager says: 'Digital skills aren't really relevant for this role. They just need to be good at the core functions.' Meanwhile, a departing staff member who was a digital champion leaves a significant gap in the team's digital capability.

response_options.text: We recognise this is a gap. We've started reviewing all teaching and learning role profiles to include digital competency requirements
response_options.explanation: Purposeful review of role profiles to embed digital requirements indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: Digital skills are important but they're something people develop on the job. We don't need to specify them in recruitment
response_options.explanation: Assuming digital skills will develop organically is the Incidental pattern. The attractive nuisance is that this sounds like a reasonable, flexible approach

response_options.text: All our teaching and learning role profiles now include digital competencies and we assess them at interview
response_options.explanation: Embedding digital in recruitment indicates Intentional or above

response_options.text: We don't currently include digital skills in role profiles for teaching and learning positions
response_options.explanation: Absence of digital in role profiles is characteristic of Incidental

scenario_text: Your university has been running digital skills training for academic staff for two years. Attendance is good in some departments but poor in others. A few departments have transformed their practice while most continue as before. Performance reviews do not assess digital capability. You are asked whether digital skills development is working.

response_options.text: Absolutely. Training attendance is strong and we've seen real transformation in our leading departments
response_options.explanation: Training attendance with patchy uptake and no integration into performance management is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is pointing to leading departments as evidence of institutional maturity

response_options.text: We've made a good start but digital competencies aren't yet embedded in performance review, career pathways, or promotion criteria across the institution
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition that development is not yet embedded in HR processes describes Intentional

response_options.text: Digital competencies are integrated into our PDR process. Development pathways exist at every career stage. Innovation is recognised in promotion criteria
response_options.explanation: Embedded in HR processes and career pathways indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We've mandated digital training completion for all academic staff and track compliance centrally
response_options.explanation: Mandatory compliance training can generate resentment rather than culture change. Mandated attendance without HR embedding is still Intentional

scenario_text: A head of department at your university approaches you saying their team needs more digital skills support. They've been relying on one team member who is the 'digital person' for all technology-related work. When that person is on leave, digital projects stall. They ask what the institution offers.

response_options.text: We have a comprehensive programme but capability tends to concentrate in enthusiasts. We haven't yet built distributed competence across all teams
response_options.explanation: Champion-dependency describes Intentional even with good programmes

response_options.text: Our competency framework ensures all staff develop digital skills as part of their role. No team should depend on a single person
response_options.explanation: Institutional competency framework preventing single-person dependency indicates Integrated

response_options.text: That's exactly what our community of practice and digital champions network is designed to address. We support knowledge sharing across teams
response_options.explanation: A champions network can address symptoms but not root cause. If capability remains concentrated in designated champions, this is Intentional

response_options.text: We have some training available. I'd suggest sending a couple of their team on the next session
response_options.explanation: Ad-hoc training referral without systematic capability building is Intentional

scenario_text: Your university has invested heavily in developing digital capabilities across academic staff. Competency frameworks are embedded in HR processes, communities of practice are active, and satisfaction is high. You are asked whether the institution should now focus elsewhere or continue investing.

response_options.text: Our development programmes are comprehensive and well-attended. We can now focus investment elsewhere and maintain current provision
response_options.explanation: Good institutional provision maintained centrally is Integrated. Optimised culture is self-sustaining and peer-driven, not dependent on continued central provision

response_options.text: Development has become largely self-sustaining. Staff drive their own learning and peer development. We should invest in supporting that culture, not controlling it
response_options.explanation: Self-sustaining, peer-driven development culture indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're well-established internally. We should now contribute to sector workforce development by sharing our frameworks and offering training to other institutions
response_options.explanation: Sector contribution indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We need to maintain our investment. Without continued institutional programmes, capability will erode
response_options.explanation: Dependency on institutional programmes for capability maintenance indicates Integrated not Optimised

scenario_text: Your university is known for strong digital skills among academic staff. A peer institution contacts you asking to learn from your approach. You also notice that your digital innovation often follows trends set by two or three leading institutions rather than originating internally.

response_options.text: We're happy to share our approach. We've developed it by carefully studying and adapting best practice from leading institutions
response_options.explanation: Adapting others' best practice is Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that sharing your adapted approach feels like leadership

response_options.text: We generate original approaches that others adopt. Our staff regularly publish and present on novel digital practices they've developed
response_options.explanation: Originating novel approaches adopted by peers indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're strong implementers of established good practice. We aren't really generating new approaches that others follow
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition of implementing vs leading is Integrated

response_options.text: Our approach is distinctive and recognised. We contribute to sector thinking through advisory roles and published research on digital workforce development
response_options.explanation: Sustained sector contribution through advisory and publication indicates Optimised

scenario_text: Your university recently discovered that five departments are using three different tools for essentially the same teaching and learning function. No one made a decision to standardise, and each department chose independently. IT maintains all three but has raised concerns about sustainability.

response_options.text: This shows our departments are proactive about adopting technology. We support local autonomy in tool selection
response_options.explanation: Framing fragmentation as autonomy is the Incidental attractive nuisance. Uncoordinated duplication is not empowerment

response_options.text: We've identified this as a problem and are developing a technology roadmap to rationalise and integrate our teaching and learning systems
response_options.explanation: Developing a purposeful roadmap indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: This has happened because we don't have an institutional technology strategy for teaching and learning. Departments filled gaps independently
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition of uncoordinated adoption is Incidental

response_options.text: We have an approved technology roadmap and procurement policy requiring architectural review. New tools must align with our standards
response_options.explanation: An approved roadmap with procurement governance indicates Intentional

scenario_text: IT at your university has been asked to prepare a technology investment case for teaching and learning. When they attempt to map the current landscape, they find no documentation of what systems are in use across departments, who owns them, or how they connect.

response_options.text: We know our landscape is complex. We've commissioned an audit and will use it to develop a roadmap with integration priorities
response_options.explanation: Commissioning an audit to inform purposeful planning indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We have a comprehensive, documented technology landscape with identified integration points and investment priorities
response_options.explanation: If true, this indicates Intentional or above

response_options.text: Our systems work fine individually. We don't really need a map because each department manages its own technology effectively
response_options.explanation: Defending fragmentation as departmental effectiveness is Incidental

response_options.text: We recognise we have limited visibility of our technology landscape and it's never been formally documented
response_options.explanation: Undocumented, unmanaged technology landscape is Incidental

scenario_text: Your university has invested in modernising its VLE and assessment platform and migrated to cloud hosting. Single sign-on connects the main platforms. However, a review reveals that several key data flows between systems are manual, the architecture has no formal governance, and procurement still happens without architectural review in some faculties.

response_options.text: We've achieved integration. Our core systems are in the cloud with SSO and our main platforms are connected
response_options.explanation: Cloud hosting and SSO are positive steps but manual data flows, ungoverned architecture, and uncontrolled procurement indicate Intentional. The attractive nuisance is equating modernisation with integration

response_options.text: We've made good progress on modernisation but we haven't yet achieved full architectural governance and automated data flows across all systems
response_options.explanation: Recognising the gap between modernisation and integration accurately describes Intentional

response_options.text: All our teaching and learning systems are governed by enterprise architecture standards, connected through APIs, and procurement requires architectural review institution-wide
response_options.explanation: Comprehensive architecture governance with API integration indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We have a full integration platform with service level monitoring, planned refresh cycles, and joint IT-domain governance
response_options.explanation: Integration platform with comprehensive governance indicates Integrated

scenario_text: All faculties at your university use the same VLE and assessment platform. IT mandated this five years ago. However, faculties configure the system differently, there are no shared standards, and the system was chosen by IT without consulting domain experts. You are asked whether this represents integrated technology.

response_options.text: Absolutely. Everyone uses the same platform, which means our technology is integrated for teaching and learning
response_options.explanation: Mandated shared platform without configuration standards, domain input, or architectural governance is technology standardisation not integration

response_options.text: We have a shared platform but we recognise it was an IT-led decision without domain governance. We're now establishing joint governance with configuration standards
response_options.explanation: Recognising the governance gap and working to address it describes Intentional moving toward Integrated

response_options.text: Our shared platform has institution-wide configuration standards developed jointly by IT and domain stakeholders, with regular review
response_options.explanation: Jointly governed platform with shared standards indicates Integrated

response_options.text: The platform was chosen without faculty input and each faculty uses it differently. It creates as many problems as it solves
response_options.explanation: Mandated without governance is not integrated

scenario_text: Your university has well-governed, integrated technology for teaching and learning. A new technology emerges that could significantly enhance teaching and learning capability. Several peer institutions are evaluating it. You are asked how to respond.

response_options.text: We should wait to see how peers implement it and learn from their experience before committing resources
response_options.explanation: Waiting to learn from peers is reactive, characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that this feels prudent

response_options.text: Our sandbox environment is already being used to evaluate this. Our technology futures panel assessed it three months ago and we have a pilot planned
response_options.explanation: Proactive assessment through established processes indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We should commission a thorough evaluation and develop a business case before proceeding
response_options.explanation: Thorough evaluation is good practice but reactive evaluation of already-visible technologies is Integrated

response_options.text: We anticipated this development through our horizon scanning. We've already published a position paper and are advising sector bodies on implementation approaches
response_options.explanation: Anticipation through horizon scanning and sector leadership indicates Optimised

scenario_text: Your university achieves 99.5% uptime on its VLE and assessment platform and has strong user satisfaction scores. A vendor invites you to present your technology approach at their annual conference as a customer success story. You are asked whether this means you are sector-leading.

response_options.text: High availability and vendor recognition confirms we are Optimised in technology for teaching and learning
response_options.explanation: Reliability is Integrated. Vendor marketing invitations are not the same as sector-recognised innovation and leadership

response_options.text: We're well-run but reliable operations are table stakes. We need to ask whether our architecture enables innovation and whether we're advancing practice beyond our own institution
response_options.explanation: Recognising that reliability alone is not sector leadership accurately assesses Integrated

response_options.text: Our architecture is extensible, we have sandbox environments, we run regular technology innovation cycles, and peer institutions adopt our published architectural patterns
response_options.explanation: Innovation capacity and adopted patterns indicate Optimised

response_options.text: We're early adopters of new features and always among the first to upgrade to the latest version
response_options.explanation: Early adoption of vendor releases is not the same as architectural innovation and sector contribution

scenario_text: Your university needs to produce a report on digital teaching and learning activity for a regulatory body. The data team discovers that relevant metrics are held in spreadsheets by individual departments, each using different definitions and formats. Compiling the report takes three weeks of manual work.

response_options.text: We meet all our statutory reporting requirements. Our data management is adequate for external purposes
response_options.explanation: Meeting statutory requirements through manual compilation is Incidental. The attractive nuisance is equating compliance with data maturity

response_options.text: We've identified our core student and learning datasets, standardised definitions, and started systematic collection to replace departmental spreadsheets
response_options.explanation: Standardised definitions and systematic collection indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Our student and learning data is fragmented across departments with no standard definitions. We rely on manual compilation for reporting
response_options.explanation: Fragmented data with manual compilation is Incidental

response_options.text: Our student and learning data is centrally managed with standardised definitions, automated collection, and dashboards. The report could be produced in hours
response_options.explanation: This describes at least Intentional

scenario_text: A dean at your university wants to make a data-informed decision about digital investment in teaching and learning. When they ask for relevant data, they are told it doesn't exist in any centralised form and would need to be collected manually from multiple sources.

response_options.text: Our student and learning data is comprehensive and available through self-service dashboards
response_options.explanation: This would indicate at least Intentional

response_options.text: We don't currently have systematic data collection for teaching and learning. We're planning to implement it
response_options.explanation: No systematic collection is Incidental

response_options.text: We collect good data but it sits in different systems and teams. We're working on integrating it into a central platform
response_options.explanation: Purposeful integration of existing data indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Deans should be able to make these decisions based on their professional judgment. They shouldn't need a dashboard for everything
response_options.explanation: Dismissing the need for data-informed decisions is characteristic of Incidental. The attractive nuisance is framing this as valuing professional expertise

scenario_text: Your university has built dashboards for student and learning data and drafted a data governance policy. However, a data quality audit reveals significant inconsistencies: 30% of key fields have missing or incorrect data, governance compliance varies by department, and most committees still make decisions without consulting the available data.

response_options.text: We have dashboards and governance in place. Data quality will improve over time as people get used to the new systems
response_options.explanation: Dashboards and policy without quality management and actual use for decision-making is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is expecting passive improvement

response_options.text: We've built the infrastructure but haven't yet achieved reliable quality, consistent governance, or data-informed decision-making across the institution
response_options.explanation: Recognising the gap between infrastructure and institutional adoption accurately describes Intentional

response_options.text: Our data quality is actively managed with regular audits, governance is operational with compliance monitoring, and committee papers routinely include data analysis
response_options.explanation: Active quality management, operational governance, and routine data use indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We need to prioritise data quality remediation and embed data use in committee processes before we can call our data mature
response_options.explanation: Identifying remediation needs accurately places the institution at Intentional

scenario_text: The planning department at your university produces excellent student and learning reports. However, when you investigate, you find these reports are produced by a small specialist team. Faculty and department leaders do not have self-service access and must request custom reports each time. Data governance relies on the planning team's expertise rather than institutional processes.

response_options.text: Our reporting is excellent and the planning team ensures data quality. This is an effective model
response_options.explanation: Expert-dependent reporting without self-service or institutional governance is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is that high-quality output feels like maturity

response_options.text: We produce good reports but data capability is concentrated in one team. We need to democratise access and formalise governance institutionally
response_options.explanation: Expert dependency without distributed access is Intentional

response_options.text: Self-service analytics are available to authorised users across the institution with institutional data governance ensuring quality
response_options.explanation: Distributed access with institutional governance indicates Integrated

response_options.text: Leaders can access data through an institutional analytics platform with training support and defined governance roles across all units
response_options.explanation: Institutional platform with governance indicates Integrated

scenario_text: Your university has comprehensive, well-governed student and learning data with institution-wide dashboards. A vendor offers an AI-powered predictive analytics tool. The PVC Education is excited and wants to implement it immediately, claiming it will make the institution Optimised.

response_options.text: Implementing AI analytics on our well-governed data will make us sector-leading immediately
response_options.explanation: Tool adoption does not equal maturity. Optimised requires proven impact, continuous improvement, and sector contribution, not just tool acquisition

response_options.text: We should pilot the tool, evaluate impact against outcomes, and publish our findings. If it works, we'll iterate and share our methodology
response_options.explanation: Evidence-based evaluation with publication and continuous improvement indicates Optimised approach

response_options.text: We already use predictive models validated against outcomes with documented impact. We'd evaluate this tool against our existing capabilities
response_options.explanation: Existing validated predictive capabilities with impact evidence indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We should implement it carefully with proper evaluation. AI tools need to be properly governed before deployment
response_options.explanation: Careful implementation with governance is good Integrated practice, not Optimised

scenario_text: A sector body asks your university to contribute to developing new data standards for teaching and learning. You currently have strong internal data governance but have not previously engaged with sector-level data practice.

response_options.text: We'd be delighted to contribute. Our data governance for teaching and learning is strong internally and we're ready to share our approaches
response_options.explanation: Willingness and readiness to contribute to sector standards indicates movement toward Optimised

response_options.text: We're confident our internal data practice is good but we should focus on maintaining what we have rather than taking on sector work
response_options.explanation: Internal focus without sector contribution is Integrated

response_options.text: We've been contributing to sector data standards for several years and our governance framework has been adopted by three peer institutions
response_options.explanation: Sustained contribution with peer adoption indicates established Optimised

response_options.text: We benchmark our data governance against the sector body's existing standards to ensure we meet best practice
response_options.explanation: Benchmarking against others' standards is consuming not contributing. The attractive nuisance is that benchmarking feels like sector engagement

scenario_text: Your university invested in VLE, online assessment, and learning analytics two years ago. Usage data (where available) shows that only 30% of academics and students regularly use the core features, and fewer than 10% use advanced capabilities. Most academics and students continue with previous manual or paper-based approaches.

response_options.text: We've made the investment and the tools are available. People will adopt at their own pace
response_options.explanation: Availability without promotion of adoption is Incidental. The attractive nuisance is framing passive availability as a strategy

response_options.text: We've launched a training programme with minimum usage expectations and we're tracking adoption rates institution-wide
response_options.explanation: Purposeful promotion with training and tracking indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Adoption is low and we don't have a plan to address it. The tools are there but people haven't taken to them
response_options.explanation: Unaddressed low adoption is Incidental

response_options.text: Usage is high and consistent. Over 80% of academics and students regularly use both basic and advanced features
response_options.explanation: This would indicate at least Intentional but contradicts the scenario

scenario_text: A few academics and students at your university have developed impressive workflows using VLE, online assessment, and learning analytics and have been nominated for an innovation award. Meanwhile, their immediate colleagues continue using older methods. No one has been asked to adopt the innovative approaches more widely.

response_options.text: Our award nominees demonstrate excellent utilisation across the institution
response_options.explanation: Individual excellence is the Incidental pattern. The attractive nuisance is pointing to champions as evidence of institutional utilisation

response_options.text: We've identified these innovators and are using their approaches to develop institutional training and minimum standards for all academics and students
response_options.explanation: Converting individual innovation into institutional programme indicates Intentional

response_options.text: These individuals found their own way. We haven't yet developed an institutional approach to promoting consistent utilisation
response_options.explanation: Individual adoption without institutional promotion is Incidental

response_options.text: We have minimum standards for tool usage and consistent adoption is monitored across the institution
response_options.explanation: Institutional standards with monitoring indicates at least Intentional

scenario_text: Your university has been actively promoting adoption of VLE, online assessment, and learning analytics with training programmes and published expectations. Adoption has risen to 65% for basic features, with three faculties at over 80% and two below 40%. Impact on outcomes is not measured.

response_options.text: Adoption is growing strongly. We're approaching integrated utilisation across the institution
response_options.explanation: Significant variation (40-80%) across faculties and no impact measurement is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is that average growth masks inconsistency

response_options.text: Adoption is growing but not yet consistent. We need institution-wide standards, measurement of outcomes, and intervention in lagging areas
response_options.explanation: Inconsistent adoption without impact measurement is Intentional

response_options.text: Adoption is consistently above 80% across all units, we measure impact on outcomes, and user feedback informs tool optimisation
response_options.explanation: Consistent high adoption with impact measurement indicates Integrated

response_options.text: All core teaching and learning processes run on digital workflows and we can demonstrate improvement in outcomes attributable to tool utilisation
response_options.explanation: Digital workflows as standard with demonstrated impact indicates Integrated

scenario_text: Several departments at your university report that they have 'gone fully digital' for teaching and learning processes. However, an audit reveals that while forms are digital, they are printed out for review, approvals happen by email rather than through the system, and data entry is duplicated across platforms.

response_options.text: We've digitised our processes. All our forms and records are digital now
response_options.explanation: Digitising the form without digitising the workflow is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is equating digital forms with digital processes

response_options.text: We've digitised inputs but not workflows. True utilisation means end-to-end digital processes without manual intervention
response_options.explanation: Recognising partial digitisation accurately describes Intentional

response_options.text: Our processes run end-to-end digitally with no paper fallbacks, automated routing, and single data entry
response_options.explanation: End-to-end digital workflows indicate Integrated

response_options.text: We've not digitised our processes yet. Most work is still paper-based
response_options.explanation: This understates the scenario which describes partial digitisation

scenario_text: Your university has consistent, high utilisation of VLE, online assessment, and learning analytics across all units. A vendor approaches you asking to feature your institution as a case study for how well you use their product. You are asked whether this means your utilisation is Optimised.

response_options.text: Vendor recognition confirms we are sector-leading in utilisation of teaching and learning tools
response_options.explanation: Vendor case studies are marketing tools, not independent assessment. Consistent usage of a product as intended is Integrated, not innovation

response_options.text: We use the tools well as designed. But Optimised utilisation means our users innovate new use cases and drive continuous improvement beyond standard deployment
response_options.explanation: Distinguishing standard effective use from innovation-driven optimisation is accurate

response_options.text: Our users have developed novel applications of these tools that the vendor has incorporated into their product roadmap. We continuously optimise based on usage analytics
response_options.explanation: User innovation influencing vendor roadmaps and continuous optimisation indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We regularly present at user conferences sharing innovative workflows our academics and students have developed, and peer institutions adopt our configurations
response_options.explanation: Innovative workflows adopted by peers indicates Optimised

scenario_text: Your university monitors utilisation of VLE, online assessment, and learning analytics through monthly reports. Adoption is consistently above 85% for core features. Users report high satisfaction. A review asks whether there is anything more to achieve.

response_options.text: We've achieved consistent high utilisation. We should maintain current levels and focus investment elsewhere
response_options.explanation: Maintenance of current utilisation is Integrated. Optimised means continuous improvement and innovation, not steady-state management

response_options.text: We should move from monitoring adoption to analysing usage patterns to identify optimisation opportunities and measuring impact on outcomes
response_options.explanation: Moving from adoption monitoring to optimisation and impact measurement indicates Optimised thinking

response_options.text: Our users already drive innovation. We analyse usage patterns in real-time, users contribute novel workflows, and we quantify impact on outcomes
response_options.explanation: User-driven innovation with analytics and impact quantification indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We should push adoption of advanced features to increase the 85% further
response_options.explanation: Pursuing higher adoption of existing features is still an Integrated activity, not innovation-driven optimisation

scenario_text: Your university has been responding to digital demands in research on a case-by-case basis. Several departments have adopted different tools independently. The senior leadership team has recently discussed the need for a more coordinated approach. A deputy vice-chancellor asks you: 'Where are we on digital strategy for research?'

response_options.text: We have a clear digital strategy for research that was approved last year and is being implemented across all faculties
response_options.explanation: This would indicate Intentional if true, but the scenario describes no approved strategy

response_options.text: We recognise the need and are actively developing a digital strategy for research with identified priorities and a governance proposal
response_options.explanation: Active development of a purposeful strategy with governance indicates transition toward Intentional

response_options.text: We've been meaning to write a strategy but haven't found the time. Meanwhile, departments are managing things in their own way
response_options.explanation: Acknowledged need without action and devolved ad-hoc activity is Incidental

response_options.text: Our institutional strategic plan mentions digital transformation and we reference that when departments ask for guidance
response_options.explanation: A passing mention in a broader strategy without specific objectives, owners, or resources for research is not a purposeful strategy. This is the 'we have a plan' attractive nuisance

scenario_text: Your university's board has asked for an update on how digital technology supports research. You discover that while several successful digital initiatives exist across the institution, they were each initiated by individual champions with no central coordination. The board wants to know what the institutional approach is.

response_options.text: We have a coordinated institutional approach with a strategy document, dedicated budget, and a committee overseeing digital in research
response_options.explanation: This describes Intentional with formal strategy, resources, and governance

response_options.text: We have some excellent initiatives and we're now developing a formal strategy to bring them together under a coherent plan
response_options.explanation: Transitioning from ad-hoc to purposeful planning indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We have a lot of innovative activity happening organically. Our approach is to let a thousand flowers bloom and learn from what works
response_options.explanation: Framing lack of strategy as deliberate emergent innovation is a common attractive nuisance. Organic activity without coordination is Incidental

response_options.text: We don't really have an institutional approach yet. Individual departments have done their own thing based on local needs
response_options.explanation: Honest acknowledgement of no institutional approach is Incidental

scenario_text: Your university approved a digital research strategy 18 months ago. The strategy has clear objectives and a steering group meets quarterly. However, implementation varies dramatically across faculties. Two faculties are well advanced, three have barely started, and the remaining faculties fall somewhere in between. A new PVC asks how well the strategy is being implemented.

response_options.text: The strategy is fully embedded. All faculties have adopted it and are implementing it consistently with local adaptation
response_options.explanation: This would indicate Integrated if true, but the scenario contradicts this

response_options.text: We have strong pockets of implementation and we're working to bring all faculties up to the standard of our leading areas
response_options.explanation: 'Strong pockets' with inconsistent implementation across the institution is characteristic of Intentional. The attractive nuisance is that activity in multiple locations feels like integration

response_options.text: Implementation is uneven. We have the strategy but we haven't yet achieved consistent cross-institutional adoption with proper governance and accountability
response_options.explanation: Honest assessment of uneven implementation describes Intentional

response_options.text: All faculties have operational plans that reference the institutional strategy, with locally adapted targets, and we report on progress to the board termly
response_options.explanation: Faculty-level plans aligned to institutional strategy with regular reporting indicates Integrated

scenario_text: Your university has invested in a central digital research team of six staff who develop and support digital initiatives. The team runs projects across faculties, but each project requires negotiation with individual faculty leaders for access and cooperation. The team reports to the PVC Research but has no formal authority over faculty-level decisions.

response_options.text: Having a dedicated central team with a clear reporting line shows we have an integrated approach to digital research
response_options.explanation: A central team without governance authority over faculties and without faculty-level adoption of institutional strategy operates in an Intentional model. The attractive nuisance is equating central team existence with integration

response_options.text: We have purposeful investment in digital research but the central team operates somewhat independently from faculty planning. We need stronger governance to achieve integration
response_options.explanation: Purposeful investment without cross-institutional governance is accurately Intentional

response_options.text: The central team's work is governed by a cross-institutional board with faculty representation, and faculty plans are required to align with the digital strategy
response_options.explanation: If this were true it would indicate Integrated, but the scenario describes a team negotiating cooperation

response_options.text: Our digital research activity is still at an early stage with no real coordination between the centre and faculties
response_options.explanation: This understates the scenario, which does describe purposeful investment

scenario_text: Your university has a well-functioning digital research strategy that is implemented consistently across all faculties. Governance is strong, KPIs are reported regularly, and the institution has achieved solid results. The PVC Research wants to know whether the institution can now be considered sector-leading.

response_options.text: We regularly benchmark against Russell Group peers and ensure our approach matches best practice. We've adopted several approaches we learned from peer institutions
response_options.explanation: Benchmarking by adopting approaches from others is characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that benchmarking activity feels like sector leadership, but copying good practice is not the same as setting it

response_options.text: We review our strategy annually based on data, run a horizon scanning function, publish our approaches, and other institutions regularly visit to learn from us
response_options.explanation: Evidence-based annual review, horizon scanning, publication, and peer recognition indicates Optimised

response_options.text: Our implementation is strong and consistent but we recognise we're implementing established good practice rather than innovating ahead of the sector
response_options.explanation: Honest assessment of implementing good practice without leading innovation is Integrated

response_options.text: We've won a national award for one of our digital research initiatives and were featured in a trade publication
response_options.explanation: A single award for a specific initiative does not indicate systematic sector leadership. The attractive nuisance is equating one recognition with Optimised maturity

scenario_text: Your university has strong digital research governance and consistent implementation. The sector is now grappling with a new technological development that could significantly impact research. Several peer institutions are starting to respond.

response_options.text: We formed an expert panel six months ago to assess the implications and have already piloted approaches. We published a briefing paper that three peer institutions have since adopted
response_options.explanation: Proactive assessment, early piloting, and sector contribution through publication indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're watching what leading institutions are doing and plan to adopt best practice once it becomes clearer what works
response_options.explanation: Waiting to adopt others' practices is reactive benchmarking, characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that this feels prudent and strategic

response_options.text: We've established a task force to develop our response and are developing a pilot programme informed by sector guidance
response_options.explanation: Developing a response informed by others indicates Integrated responding effectively, not Optimised leading

response_options.text: We've been preparing for this for over a year through our horizon scanning process and have an institutional position and implementation plan ready
response_options.explanation: Anticipating the development through horizon scanning indicates Optimised proactive strategic maturity

scenario_text: Your university is assessing digital skills readiness among researchers. A survey reveals that 15% of researchers are highly digitally capable and actively innovating, while 60% use basic digital tools but avoid anything more advanced. The remaining 25% actively resist using digital tools. No institutional development programme for digital skills in research exists.

response_options.text: We clearly have digital capability. 15% of our researchers are highly skilled and leading innovation in research
response_options.explanation: Concentrated expertise in a small minority without institutional development is the hallmark of Incidental. The attractive nuisance is celebrating individual champions as institutional capability

response_options.text: We need to start investing in digital skills for researchers. We're planning a development programme targeting the 60% in the middle
response_options.explanation: Planning purposeful investment in workforce development indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We don't have an institutional programme. Skills are developed through informal peer learning and self-study
response_options.explanation: Informal, self-directed development without institutional programme is Incidental

response_options.text: We've launched a targeted digital capabilities programme for researchers with modules mapped to role requirements, and we're tracking participation
response_options.explanation: A targeted, tracked programme indicates Intentional

scenario_text: Your university is recruiting for a senior role in research. The job description does not mention digital competencies. The hiring manager says: 'Digital skills aren't really relevant for this role. They just need to be good at the core functions.' Meanwhile, a departing staff member who was a digital champion leaves a significant gap in the team's digital capability.

response_options.text: We recognise this is a gap. We've started reviewing all research role profiles to include digital competency requirements
response_options.explanation: Purposeful review of role profiles to embed digital requirements indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: Digital skills are important but they're something people develop on the job. We don't need to specify them in recruitment
response_options.explanation: Assuming digital skills will develop organically is the Incidental pattern. The attractive nuisance is that this sounds like a reasonable, flexible approach

response_options.text: All our research role profiles now include digital competencies and we assess them at interview
response_options.explanation: Embedding digital in recruitment indicates Intentional or above

response_options.text: We don't currently include digital skills in role profiles for research positions
response_options.explanation: Absence of digital in role profiles is characteristic of Incidental

scenario_text: Your university has been running digital skills training for researchers for two years. Attendance is good in some departments but poor in others. A few departments have transformed their practice while most continue as before. Performance reviews do not assess digital capability. You are asked whether digital skills development is working.

response_options.text: Absolutely. Training attendance is strong and we've seen real transformation in our leading departments
response_options.explanation: Training attendance with patchy uptake and no integration into performance management is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is pointing to leading departments as evidence of institutional maturity

response_options.text: We've made a good start but digital competencies aren't yet embedded in performance review, career pathways, or promotion criteria across the institution
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition that development is not yet embedded in HR processes describes Intentional

response_options.text: Digital competencies are integrated into our PDR process. Development pathways exist at every career stage. Innovation is recognised in promotion criteria
response_options.explanation: Embedded in HR processes and career pathways indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We've mandated digital training completion for all researchers and track compliance centrally
response_options.explanation: Mandatory compliance training can generate resentment rather than culture change. Mandated attendance without HR embedding is still Intentional

scenario_text: A head of department at your university approaches you saying their team needs more digital skills support. They've been relying on one team member who is the 'digital person' for all technology-related work. When that person is on leave, digital projects stall. They ask what the institution offers.

response_options.text: We have a comprehensive programme but capability tends to concentrate in enthusiasts. We haven't yet built distributed competence across all teams
response_options.explanation: Champion-dependency describes Intentional even with good programmes

response_options.text: Our competency framework ensures all staff develop digital skills as part of their role. No team should depend on a single person
response_options.explanation: Institutional competency framework preventing single-person dependency indicates Integrated

response_options.text: That's exactly what our community of practice and digital champions network is designed to address. We support knowledge sharing across teams
response_options.explanation: A champions network can address symptoms but not root cause. If capability remains concentrated in designated champions, this is Intentional

response_options.text: We have some training available. I'd suggest sending a couple of their team on the next session
response_options.explanation: Ad-hoc training referral without systematic capability building is Intentional

scenario_text: Your university has invested heavily in developing digital capabilities across researchers. Competency frameworks are embedded in HR processes, communities of practice are active, and satisfaction is high. You are asked whether the institution should now focus elsewhere or continue investing.

response_options.text: Our development programmes are comprehensive and well-attended. We can now focus investment elsewhere and maintain current provision
response_options.explanation: Good institutional provision maintained centrally is Integrated. Optimised culture is self-sustaining and peer-driven, not dependent on continued central provision

response_options.text: Development has become largely self-sustaining. Staff drive their own learning and peer development. We should invest in supporting that culture, not controlling it
response_options.explanation: Self-sustaining, peer-driven development culture indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're well-established internally. We should now contribute to sector workforce development by sharing our frameworks and offering training to other institutions
response_options.explanation: Sector contribution indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We need to maintain our investment. Without continued institutional programmes, capability will erode
response_options.explanation: Dependency on institutional programmes for capability maintenance indicates Integrated not Optimised

scenario_text: Your university is known for strong digital skills among researchers. A peer institution contacts you asking to learn from your approach. You also notice that your digital innovation often follows trends set by two or three leading institutions rather than originating internally.

response_options.text: We're happy to share our approach. We've developed it by carefully studying and adapting best practice from leading institutions
response_options.explanation: Adapting others' best practice is Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that sharing your adapted approach feels like leadership

response_options.text: We generate original approaches that others adopt. Our staff regularly publish and present on novel digital practices they've developed
response_options.explanation: Originating novel approaches adopted by peers indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We're strong implementers of established good practice. We aren't really generating new approaches that others follow
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition of implementing vs leading is Integrated

response_options.text: Our approach is distinctive and recognised. We contribute to sector thinking through advisory roles and published research on digital workforce development
response_options.explanation: Sustained sector contribution through advisory and publication indicates Optimised

scenario_text: Your university recently discovered that five departments are using three different tools for essentially the same research function. No one made a decision to standardise, and each department chose independently. IT maintains all three but has raised concerns about sustainability.

response_options.text: This shows our departments are proactive about adopting technology. We support local autonomy in tool selection
response_options.explanation: Framing fragmentation as autonomy is the Incidental attractive nuisance. Uncoordinated duplication is not empowerment

response_options.text: We've identified this as a problem and are developing a technology roadmap to rationalise and integrate our research systems
response_options.explanation: Developing a purposeful roadmap indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: This has happened because we don't have an institutional technology strategy for research. Departments filled gaps independently
response_options.explanation: Honest recognition of uncoordinated adoption is Incidental

response_options.text: We have an approved technology roadmap and procurement policy requiring architectural review. New tools must align with our standards
response_options.explanation: An approved roadmap with procurement governance indicates Intentional

scenario_text: IT at your university has been asked to prepare a technology investment case for research. When they attempt to map the current landscape, they find no documentation of what systems are in use across departments, who owns them, or how they connect.

response_options.text: We know our landscape is complex. We've commissioned an audit and will use it to develop a roadmap with integration priorities
response_options.explanation: Commissioning an audit to inform purposeful planning indicates movement toward Intentional

response_options.text: We have a comprehensive, documented technology landscape with identified integration points and investment priorities
response_options.explanation: If true, this indicates Intentional or above

response_options.text: Our systems work fine individually. We don't really need a map because each department manages its own technology effectively
response_options.explanation: Defending fragmentation as departmental effectiveness is Incidental

response_options.text: We recognise we have limited visibility of our technology landscape and it's never been formally documented
response_options.explanation: Undocumented, unmanaged technology landscape is Incidental

scenario_text: Your university has invested in modernising its research computing and data storage and migrated to cloud hosting. Single sign-on connects the main platforms. However, a review reveals that several key data flows between systems are manual, the architecture has no formal governance, and procurement still happens without architectural review in some faculties.

response_options.text: We've achieved integration. Our core systems are in the cloud with SSO and our main platforms are connected
response_options.explanation: Cloud hosting and SSO are positive steps but manual data flows, ungoverned architecture, and uncontrolled procurement indicate Intentional. The attractive nuisance is equating modernisation with integration

response_options.text: We've made good progress on modernisation but we haven't yet achieved full architectural governance and automated data flows across all systems
response_options.explanation: Recognising the gap between modernisation and integration accurately describes Intentional

response_options.text: All our research systems are governed by enterprise architecture standards, connected through APIs, and procurement requires architectural review institution-wide
response_options.explanation: Comprehensive architecture governance with API integration indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We have a full integration platform with service level monitoring, planned refresh cycles, and joint IT-domain governance
response_options.explanation: Integration platform with comprehensive governance indicates Integrated

scenario_text: All faculties at your university use the same research computing and data storage. IT mandated this five years ago. However, faculties configure the system differently, there are no shared standards, and the system was chosen by IT without consulting domain experts. You are asked whether this represents integrated technology.

response_options.text: Absolutely. Everyone uses the same platform, which means our technology is integrated for research
response_options.explanation: Mandated shared platform without configuration standards, domain input, or architectural governance is technology standardisation not integration

response_options.text: We have a shared platform but we recognise it was an IT-led decision without domain governance. We're now establishing joint governance with configuration standards
response_options.explanation: Recognising the governance gap and working to address it describes Intentional moving toward Integrated

response_options.text: Our shared platform has institution-wide configuration standards developed jointly by IT and domain stakeholders, with regular review
response_options.explanation: Jointly governed platform with shared standards indicates Integrated

response_options.text: The platform was chosen without faculty input and each faculty uses it differently. It creates as many problems as it solves
response_options.explanation: Mandated without governance is not integrated

scenario_text: Your university has well-governed, integrated technology for research. A new technology emerges that could significantly enhance research capability. Several peer institutions are evaluating it. You are asked how to respond.

response_options.text: We should wait to see how peers implement it and learn from their experience before committing resources
response_options.explanation: Waiting to learn from peers is reactive, characteristic of Integrated. The attractive nuisance is that this feels prudent

response_options.text: Our sandbox environment is already being used to evaluate this. Our technology futures panel assessed it three months ago and we have a pilot planned
response_options.explanation: Proactive assessment through established processes indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We should commission a thorough evaluation and develop a business case before proceeding
response_options.explanation: Thorough evaluation is good practice but reactive evaluation of already-visible technologies is Integrated

response_options.text: We anticipated this development through our horizon scanning. We've already published a position paper and are advising sector bodies on implementation approaches
response_options.explanation: Anticipation through horizon scanning and sector leadership indicates Optimised

scenario_text: Your university achieves 99.5% uptime on its research computing and data storage and has strong user satisfaction scores. A vendor invites you to present your technology approach at their annual conference as a customer success story. You are asked whether this means you are sector-leading.

response_options.text: High availability and vendor recognition confirms we are Optimised in technology for research
response_options.explanation: Reliability is Integrated. Vendor marketing invitations are not the same as sector-recognised innovation and leadership

response_options.text: We're well-run but reliable operations are table stakes. We need to ask whether our architecture enables innovation and whether we're advancing practice beyond our own institution
response_options.explanation: Recognising that reliability alone is not sector leadership accurately assesses Integrated

response_options.text: Our architecture is extensible, we have sandbox environments, we run regular technology innovation cycles, and peer institutions adopt our published architectural patterns
response_options.explanation: Innovation capacity and adopted patterns indicate Optimised

response_options.text: We're early adopters of new features and always among the first to upgrade to the latest version
response_options.explanation: Early adoption of vendor releases is not the same as architectural innovation and sector contribution

scenario_text: Your university needs to produce a report on digital research activity for a regulatory body. The data team discovers that relevant metrics are held in spreadsheets by individual departments, each using different definitions and formats. Compiling the report takes three weeks of manual work.

response_options.text: We meet all our statutory reporting requirements. Our data management is adequate for external purposes
response_options.explanation: Meeting statutory requirements through manual compilation is Incidental. The attractive nuisance is equating compliance with data maturity

response_options.text: We've identified our core research output and research data datasets, standardised definitions, and started systematic collection to replace departmental spreadsheets
response_options.explanation: Standardised definitions and systematic collection indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Our research output and research data data is fragmented across departments with no standard definitions. We rely on manual compilation for reporting
response_options.explanation: Fragmented data with manual compilation is Incidental

response_options.text: Our research output and research data data is centrally managed with standardised definitions, automated collection, and dashboards. The report could be produced in hours
response_options.explanation: This describes at least Intentional

scenario_text: A dean at your university wants to make a data-informed decision about digital investment in research. When they ask for relevant data, they are told it doesn't exist in any centralised form and would need to be collected manually from multiple sources.

response_options.text: Our research output and research data data is comprehensive and available through self-service dashboards
response_options.explanation: This would indicate at least Intentional

response_options.text: We don't currently have systematic data collection for research. We're planning to implement it
response_options.explanation: No systematic collection is Incidental

response_options.text: We collect good data but it sits in different systems and teams. We're working on integrating it into a central platform
response_options.explanation: Purposeful integration of existing data indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Deans should be able to make these decisions based on their professional judgment. They shouldn't need a dashboard for everything
response_options.explanation: Dismissing the need for data-informed decisions is characteristic of Incidental. The attractive nuisance is framing this as valuing professional expertise

scenario_text: Your university has built dashboards for research output and research data data and drafted a data governance policy. However, a data quality audit reveals significant inconsistencies: 30% of key fields have missing or incorrect data, governance compliance varies by department, and most committees still make decisions without consulting the available data.

response_options.text: We have dashboards and governance in place. Data quality will improve over time as people get used to the new systems
response_options.explanation: Dashboards and policy without quality management and actual use for decision-making is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is expecting passive improvement

response_options.text: We've built the infrastructure but haven't yet achieved reliable quality, consistent governance, or data-informed decision-making across the institution
response_options.explanation: Recognising the gap between infrastructure and institutional adoption accurately describes Intentional

response_options.text: Our data quality is actively managed with regular audits, governance is operational with compliance monitoring, and committee papers routinely include data analysis
response_options.explanation: Active quality management, operational governance, and routine data use indicates Integrated

response_options.text: We need to prioritise data quality remediation and embed data use in committee processes before we can call our data mature
response_options.explanation: Identifying remediation needs accurately places the institution at Intentional

scenario_text: The planning department at your university produces excellent research output and research data reports. However, when you investigate, you find these reports are produced by a small specialist team. Faculty and department leaders do not have self-service access and must request custom reports each time. Data governance relies on the planning team's expertise rather than institutional processes.

response_options.text: Our reporting is excellent and the planning team ensures data quality. This is an effective model
response_options.explanation: Expert-dependent reporting without self-service or institutional governance is Intentional. The attractive nuisance is that high-quality output feels like maturity

response_options.text: We produce good reports but data capability is concentrated in one team. We need to democratise access and formalise governance institutionally
response_options.explanation: Expert dependency without distributed access is Intentional

response_options.text: Self-service analytics are available to authorised users across the institution with institutional data governance ensuring quality
response_options.explanation: Distributed access with institutional governance indicates Integrated

response_options.text: Leaders can access data through an institutional analytics platform with training support and defined governance roles across all units
response_options.explanation: Institutional platform with governance indicates Integrated

scenario_text: Your university has comprehensive, well-governed research output and research data data with institution-wide dashboards. A vendor offers an AI-powered predictive analytics tool. The PVC Research is excited and wants to implement it immediately, claiming it will make the institution Optimised.

response_options.text: Implementing AI analytics on our well-governed data will make us sector-leading immediately
response_options.explanation: Tool adoption does not equal maturity. Optimised requires proven impact, continuous improvement, and sector contribution, not just tool acquisition

response_options.text: We should pilot the tool, evaluate impact against outcomes, and publish our findings. If it works, we'll iterate and share our methodology
response_options.explanation: Evidence-based evaluation with publication and continuous improvement indicates Optimised approach

response_options.text: We already use predictive models validated against outcomes with documented impact. We'd evaluate this tool against our existing capabilities
response_options.explanation: Existing validated predictive capabilities with impact evidence indicates Optimised

response_options.text: We should implement it carefully with proper evaluation. AI tools need to be properly governed before deployment
response_options.explanation: Careful implementation with governance is good Integrated practice, not Optimised

scenario_text: A sector body asks your university to contribute to developing new data standards for research. You currently have strong internal data governance but have not previously engaged with sector-level data practice.

response_options.text: We'd be delighted to contribute. Our data governance for research is strong internally and we're ready to share our approaches
response_options.explanation: Willingness and readiness to contribute to sector standards indicates movement toward Optimised

response_options.text: We're confident our internal data practice is good but we should focus on maintaining what we have rather than taking on sector work
response_options.explanation: Internal focus without sector contribution is Integrated

response_options.text: We've been contributing to sector data standards for several years and our governance framework has been adopted by three peer institutions
response_options.explanation: Sustained contribution with peer adoption indicates established Optimised

response_options.text: We benchmark our data governance against the sector body's existing standards to ensure we meet best practice
response_options.explanation: Benchmarking against others' standards is consuming not contributing. The attractive nuisance is that benchmarking feels like sector engagement

scenario_text: Your university invested in research data systems, computational tools, and collaboration platforms two years ago. Usage data (where available) shows that only 30% of researchers regularly use the core features, and fewer than 10% use advanced capabilities. Most researchers continue with previous manual or paper-based approaches.

response_options.text: We've made the investment and the tools are available. People will adopt at their own pace
response_options.explanation: Availability without promotion of adoption is Incidental. The attractive nuisance is framing passive availability as a strategy

response_options.text: We've launched a training programme with minimum usage expectations and we're tracking adoption rates institution-wide
response_options.explanation: Purposeful promotion with training and tracking indicates Intentional

response_options.text: Adoption is low and we don't have a plan to address it. The tools are there but people haven't taken to them
response_options.explanation: Unaddressed low adoption is Incidental

response_options.text: Usage is high and consistent. Over 80% of researchers regularly use both basic and advanced features
